bill.title: Concerning the National Collegiate Athletic Association policy for eligibility in women's sports.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution calls on the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) to revoke its transgender student-athlete eligibility policy and urges the NCAA to require its member conferences to conform to a biological sex-based policy across all sports and all divisions.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would call on the National Collegiate Athletic Association to revoke its transgender student-athlete eligibility policy and urge the NCAA to require its member conferences to conform to a biological sex-based policy across all sports and all divisions.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in college costs and rules. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing.
